group.passage: In the dry northeast of Kenya, many families make a living by raising camels and other animals. They move from place to place to find water and grass for their animals, so their children often live far from schools and libraries. In 1996, the Kenya National Library Service found a creative way to bring books to these families: it sent the books by camel. The library service already used trucks as mobile libraries in other parts of Kenya, but trucks were not a good choice in the northeast. The roads were poor, and the herders' homes were not in fixed places, so a truck could easily get stuck before reaching them. Camels, on the other hand, were already the main way people traveled in the area. The camel library started in the town of Garissa and later spread to Wajir. On a typical trip, one camel carried the books in two wooden boxes, one hanging on each side of its hump. A second camel carried a tent, and a third went along as a spare in case one of the others could not go on. When the group reached a stop, the librarians put up the tent and laid the books out on mats. Children then chose the books they wanted and borrowed them with their library cards. The camels traveled to places within about 15 kilometers of the libraries in town. The animals worked hard, but they were well cared for. The camel library served readers from Monday to Thursday. From Friday to Sunday, the camels were set free to eat and rest, and animal doctors checked them for any sign of illness. In the early years, most of the books were gifts from aid groups in other countries. For children who lived far from any school library, the sight of the camels arriving meant new stories to read.

1.explanation_zh: 第一段說肯亞東北部牧民的孩子離學校和圖書館很遠，1996 年國家圖書館服務處開始用駱駝送書；第二段說明為什麼用駱駝不用卡車；第三段說駱駝圖書館怎麼運作；第四段說駱駝如何被照顧。全文講的是用駱駝把書送給孩子的圖書館。
evidence: In 1996, the Kenya National Library Service found a creative way to bring books to these families: it sent the books by camel.
For children who lived far from any school library, the sight of the camels arriving meant new stories to read.

option_notes_zh.A: 牧民為牲畜找水和草只是第一段的背景說明。
option_notes_zh.C: 卡車容易陷住只是第二段說明「為什麼不用卡車」的理由，不是全文重點。

1.strategy_zh: 主旨題要選能涵蓋每一段的選項；第一段最後一句點出主題（用駱駝送書），後面各段都在說明它。
hints: 第一段最後一句說圖書館服務處想到什麼辦法？
第二到第四段分別說了什麼？
找能涵蓋「駱駝」「書」「孩子」的選項。

2.explanation_zh: 第二段說那裡道路很差，牧民的住處又不固定，所以卡車很容易在抵達前就陷住。也就是卡車不容易到達牧民的家。
evidence: The roads were poor, and the herders' homes were not in fixed places, so a truck could easily get stuck before reaching them.

option_notes_zh.B: 文中沒有提到卡車的價錢。
option_notes_zh.C: 文中沒有說牧民不想讓卡車靠近牲畜。
option_notes_zh.D: 文中確實說卡車在肯亞其他地方被當成行動圖書館，但那只是交代背景，不是東北部不用卡車的原因；原因在下一句。

2.strategy_zh: 問原因的題目，找 because、so 這類因果詞；文中出現過的句子不一定是答案，要看它回答的是不是題目問的「原因」。
hints: 回到第二段，找有 so 的那一句。
道路和牧民的住處有什麼問題？
D 的 other parts of Kenya 那一句是在說原因嗎？

3.explanation_zh: 同一句前半說「肯亞國家圖書館服務處想到一個有創意的方法」，冒號後的 it 用駱駝送書，做這件事的是這個服務處。
evidence: In 1996, the Kenya National Library Service found a creative way to bring books to these families: it sent the books by camel.

option_notes_zh.A: 駱駝是被用來運書的工具，句中說的是 by camel；駱駝不會自己決定「把書用駱駝送出去」。
option_notes_zh.B: 「方法」不會去送書；把 a creative way 代回 ___ sent the books by camel 說不通。
option_notes_zh.D: 東北部是地點，不會送書。

3.strategy_zh: 代名詞題把每個候選詞代回原句，看誰能做「送書」這個動作；能做動作的通常是前面的主詞。
hints: 粗體 it 在第一段最後一句，先找同一句的主詞。
誰「找到了一個有創意的方法」？
把它代回 ___ sent the books by camel，意思通嗎？

4.explanation_zh: 第四段說星期五到星期日，駱駝被放出去吃草休息，並由獸醫檢查有沒有生病的跡象。D 是這一句的改寫。
evidence: From Friday to Sunday, the camels were set free to eat and rest, and animal doctors checked them for any sign of illness.

option_notes_zh.A: 瓦吉爾是駱駝圖書館後來擴展到的地方，文中沒有說週末要把書運去那裡。
option_notes_zh.B: 第二頭駱駝載帳篷是第三段在說「出勤時」的分工；星期五到星期日駱駝是休息的。
option_notes_zh.C: 文中沒有提到把駱駝賣掉。

4.strategy_zh: 題幹有特定時間（Friday to Sunday），先找到那一句；其他選項常是文中別的時候發生的事。
hints: 在第四段找 From Friday to Sunday。
那幾天駱駝做什麼？誰來檢查牠們？
B 的帳篷出現在第三段，那是在說哪一天的事？

translation_zh.text:
在肯亞乾燥的東北部，許多家庭靠飼養駱駝和其他牲畜維生。他們為了替牲畜尋找水和草而四處遷移，所以孩子們常常住得離學校和圖書館很遠。1996 年，肯亞國家圖書館服務處想出一個有創意的方法，把書送到這些家庭手中：它用駱駝運送書本。
這個圖書館服務處在肯亞其他地方早就使用卡車當作行動圖書館，但在東北部，卡車並不是好選擇。那裡的道路很差，牧民的住處又不固定，所以卡車很容易在抵達之前就陷住。相反地，駱駝本來就是當地人主要的交通工具。
駱駝圖書館從加里薩鎮開始，後來擴展到瓦吉爾。在一趟典型的行程中，一頭駱駝用兩個木箱載書，駝峰兩側各掛一個。第二頭駱駝載帳篷，第三頭則隨行備用，以防其他駱駝無法繼續走。隊伍到達一個站點時，圖書館員會搭起帳篷，把書攤在草蓆上。孩子們接著挑選想看的書，用借書證借閱。駱駝會走到距離鎮上圖書館大約 15 公里以內的地方。
這些動物工作很辛苦，但受到很好的照顧。駱駝圖書館從星期一到星期四為讀者服務。星期五到星期日，駱駝會被放出去吃東西、休息，並由獸醫檢查有沒有生病的跡象。早年的時候，大部分的書都是其他國家的援助團體捐贈的。對當時住得離任何學校圖書館都很遠的孩子來說，看到駱駝到來，就代表有新的故事可以讀。

Started in Garissa and later spread to Wajir（核對：f2；KNLS：Wajir launched April 13th 1999）
Trucks used elsewhere in Kenya; poor roads and non-fixed homes meant trucks could get stuck（核對：f3；NDL Current Awareness CA1281、CSMonitor 1999 佐證）
Camels were the main way people traveled in the area（核對：f4；KNLS：culturally acceptable and treasured mode of transport）

One camel carried books in two wooden boxes; a second the tent; a third as a spare（核對：f5；KNLS：one camel carried two book boxes … another carried a tent, reading mat … the third camel was used as a spare）
Books laid out on mats; children borrowed with library cards（核對：f6；mats 有 KNLS（reading mat）與其他報導佐證；library cards 出自 Washington Post 1999（直接抓取 403，未能開原文，依事實單））
Camels traveled to places within about 15 km of the libraries in town（核對：f7；KNLS 官方寫 about 15 to 20 km，文中取 about 15 km，與事實單一致、與官方下限相符）

Served readers Monday–Thursday; Friday–Sunday camels set free to eat and rest and checked by vets（核對：f8；Library Philosophy and Practice（digitalcommons.unl.edu, article 2096，搜尋擷取原句）：serves readers from Mondays to Thursdays, and camels are released on Fridays to Sundays to go and feed, recuperate and are vetted for any signs of disease (KNLS 2010)）
In the early years most books were gifts from aid groups in other countries（核對：f9；出自 Washington Post 1999（403，未能開原文，依事實單）；Mail & Guardian 2000「depends largely on donations」佐證）
Numbers in passage and questions: 1996, 15 kilometers（核對：與事實單一致）
